bearings.paper_claim: Bill-level endorsement signals predict cosponsor counts: max endorser standardized eigenvector centrality coef 0.055 (SE 0.011) and endorser count coef 0.007 (SE 0.001), both p<.001, negative binomial with Congress FE, N = 6,597 House bills with supportive Dear Colleague letters, 106th-111th Congresses. Predicted cosponsors: 33 for a bill endorsed only by unconnected groups (score -0.2053) or with no endorsements; 38 with centrality 2.51 (Anti-Defamation League); 51 with centrality 7.66 (Planned Parenthood).
bearings.system_side: cosponsor_forecast.py feature list (lines 117-142) is a ridge-logistic model. It uses member-dyad features (prior sponsor affinity, prior member cosponsorships, network degree and eigenvector, NOMINATE distances, party, state, seniority, prior coservice, member on referred committee) PLUS bill-level and sponsor-level covariates (bill_committee_referrals, bill_type, policy_area, sponsor_majority_party). The analyst claim of member-dyad features only is wrong. No endorsement or outside-support feature exists (confirmed). The 265,396-row count and unscored status were not found in the repo.
bearings.code_ref: fec/lobbying/cosponsor_forecast.py:117-142 (feature list verified; no endorsement feature present)
bearings.transfer_conditions: Paper estimates are pooled across Congresses and both parties with no party or majority strata reported, so quote as UNSTRATIFIED. The outcome is a bill-level cosponsor count, not a dyad join. Any added bill-level signal must be dated before introduction. Endorsements are public pro-bill signals, but the paper does not show they reflect group influence because solicitation direction is unresolved (footnote 11). LDA counts are not a substitute under D-021.
bearings.verifier_note: Numbers, N, and table location verified against the text. Softened the system-side description, which contradicts itself (member-dyad only versus bill-level covariates in the code). Unverified: the 265,396-row count and the unscored status.

bearings.paper_claim: Passed House logit (Table 4, N = 6,597): hot bill 2.428 (SE .161), commemorative 1.386 (SE .150), majority-party sponsor 1.353 (SE .220), endorser count 0.013 (SE .004), cosponsors 0.004 (SE .001). Endorser social power is -0.035 (SE .032, ns) for passage and 0.020 (SE .031, ns) for reporting.
bearings.paper_location: Table 4 and Figure 5, pp. 177-178 (table verified on p. 177)
bearings.system_side: live_legislative_pillar.py lines 60-81 confirmed: per-category efficiency is the decay-weighted signed share of advanced bills, divided by the max absolute value across members, then percentile-blended. No majority-party, hot-bill, or salience adjustment appears in that block.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper estimates a covariate association over letter-bearing House bills pooled across 106th-111th Congresses. It is not a per-member efficiency model and says nothing about efficiency metrics. Reading the majority coefficient as showing that a raw advancement rate rewards majority status is an inference, not the paper's claim, and any adjustment is Paul's call.
bearings.verifier_note: Coefficients and N verified. Softened the interpretation: the paper reports majority status as a control association and does not show the efficiency rate is biased. Commemorative (1.386) is larger than majority (1.353), so majority is not a top-two passage predictor.

bearings.paper_claim: Stage-specific coefficients (Tables 3-4): endorser social power predicts cosponsors (0.055) but not reporting (0.020) or passage (-0.035). Endorser count predicts passage (0.013) but not reporting (0.004, ns). Cosponsor count predicts reporting (0.002, p<.01) and passage (0.004, p<.001).
bearings.system_side: legislative_effectiveness.py lines 17-28 confirmed: stages BILL, AIC, ABC, PASS, LAW; role weights; cosponsor_half_life_days 180; policy_status shadow_candidate, consistent with not activated.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper gives stage-specific coefficients on one sample of letter bills (N = 6,597) and does not argue for stage-based modelling; the stage pattern is an empirical observation only. It does not test cosponsor timing decay and gives no support for the 180-day half-life. Pooled, UNSTRATIFIED.
bearings.verifier_note: Coefficients verified. Softened the relation from supports-as-argument to empirical pattern only, since the paper makes no modelling recommendation.

bearings.paper_claim: Footnote 11 (p. 170): a member reviewing a Dear Colleague letter cannot distinguish an endorsement the member solicited from one the interest group solicited from a sponsor. P. 171: endorsers listed together on a letter may not have any interaction, and endorsements were likely pulled together by a member's office.
bearings.paper_location: Footnote 11 on p. 170; interaction passage on p. 171 (analyst cited p. 171 and p. 172; corrected here)
bearings.system_side: bill_lobbying_sidecar.py docstring (lines 10-20) confirmed: LDA filings never name the members lobbied, and the sidecar ships only a bill-level interaction total. The stronger claim that P(joined given lobbied) = 1 by construction, so the link was refuted, was NOT found in the cited code or sidecar.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper's endorsement channel is observed by members, which is a stronger channel than an LDA bill mention. Its authors leave solicitation direction unresolved, which supports caution about reading bill co-occurrence as influence. The paper does not discuss LDA filings.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper claim verified with corrected page numbers. The system-side refutation claim could not be found in the cited code; the docstring supports only the narrower point that LDA filings never name members.
